To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
privacy regulation has the effect of reducing publisher revenue by 30% and shifting business to large DSPs.

privacy regulations have a substantial effect on online advertising markets, with the effect on revenue being larger for smaller DSPs, and that the effect of privacy regulations on revenue is larger for smaller publishers.

(1) Privacy regulation has a significant negative impact on publishers; (2) Privacy regulation has no effect on the largest DSPs, but a significant positive effect on smaller DSPs; (3) In the case where one DSP has an information advantage, the impact of the regulation on the DSP with the information advantage is ambiguous, but the impact on publishers remains negative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how privacy measures in online markets affect advertising markets.
the effects of privacy regulations on online advertising markets.
understanding how privacy measures impact the structure of advertising markets and the welfare of market participants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
privacy regulations are not a panacea to privacy concerns.
privacy measures, while reducing publisher revenue and shifting it to larger DSPs, also increase competition in the online advertising market.
the effects of privacy regulations on online advertising markets are not as straightforward as they may seem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while privacy regulations reduce publisher revenue, they do not reduce the total surplus in the online advertising market.
privacy measures have a significant impact on advertising markets, with the largest impact on publishers, and that there is a significant role for first party data in the new privacy regime.
the impact of privacy regulation is highly heterogeneous, with some DSPs gaining and others losing, and that the presence of first party data can mitigate the impact of such regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while privacy regulations can have a large negative impact on publishers, the impact on DSPs is less clear.
the impact of privacy regulations on online advertising is not only substantial but also asymmetric, with large DSPs gaining market share.
privacy regulations, in general, have the unintended effect of increasing the market power of large firms.
